Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to determine and set out, under a sound legal basis and in accordance with the international treaties to which the Maldives is a party, the privileges available in the Maldives to diplomatic missions, consular posts, the specialised agencies of the United Nations and other related bodies, and other international administrative organisations established in the Maldives, and to persons belonging to those establishments; and to determine the scope of those privileges and the principles and procedures by which those privileges shall be granted.

Bill on the Privileges of Diplomatic Missions, Consular Posts and International Organisations

Chapter One
Introduction and Purpose

Introduction and title
1. (a) This is the Act that sets out the privileges available in the Maldives, in accordance with the international treaties to which the Maldives is a party, to diplomatic missions, consular posts, the specialised agencies of the United Nations and other related bodies, and other international administrative organisations established in the Maldives, and to persons belonging to those establishments.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Diplomatic Missions, Consular Posts and International Organisations (Privileges) Act".

Purpose of the Act
2. The main purpose of this Act is to achieve the following:

(a) to determine, in accordance with the Convention on Diplomatic Relations and the Convention on Consular Relations, the privileges granted to diplomatic missions and consular posts established in the Maldives, to all persons employed at those establishments, and to the members of their families forming part of their households;

[stamp] [signature]

(b) to determine, in accordance with the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the Specialised Agencies of the United Nations, the privileges granted to the specialised agencies, other related bodies and persons belonging to those establishments; and

(c) to determine the privileges granted to the international organisations specifically set out in the Act and to persons connected with those organisations.

(b) The privileges set out in subsection (a) of this section shall be granted only in respect of posts of the following categories:

(1) a representative on a board of that organisation (whether or not belonging to a foreign country), or a representative on a committee of that organisation or on any other [?] board formed under the organisation;

[stamp] [signature]

(2) a senior officer or senior official of that organisation;

(3) to a determined specific extent, experts appointed as employees of that organisation or to posts active on a mission of the organisation, or [?] or administrative members of that organisation, or employees of any other category.

Privileges that may be granted to other officers and employees

21. To implement an agreement made by the Government of the Maldives with an international organisation, the Minister may determine that the following privileges may be granted, to a specific extent determined by the Minister, to other posts connected with that organisation:

(a) privilege from legal proceedings brought against him in relation to anything he did or omitted to do in the course of performing the official duties of that post;

(b) exemption from payment of tax levied on remuneration received in the capacity of an officer or employee of that organisation.

Chapter Four
Miscellaneous

Certificate issued by the Minister

22. (a) A relevant certificate issued by the Minister, or issued under authority delegated by the Minister, shall be sufficient evidence in proving that a privilege available, under a regulation made under this Act, to a diplomatic mission, a consular post, an international organisation, or a particular post or posts is [?] a privilege available to those posts.

[stamp] [signature]

(b) A certificate issued under subsection (a) of this section shall be accepted as sufficient evidence to prove the matters set out in it.

Acting on the principle of reciprocity

23. (a) No provision of this Act shall be interpreted in a manner that prevents the Government from withdrawing the privileges granted to the citizens of a foreign country or to posts representing that country, or from refusing to grant those privileges to those posts, if that country has not granted to citizens of the Maldives or to posts representing the Maldives privileges equal to the privileges granted to the citizens of that foreign country or to posts representing that country.

(b) In circumstances where the Minister considers that the privileges granted to a diplomatic mission or consular post of the Maldives established in a foreign country, or to posts connected with that mission or post, are of a lower standard than the privileges granted under this Act to a diplomatic mission or consular post of that country established in the Maldives, or to posts connected with that mission or post, the Minister shall have the discretion to withdraw or restore the privileges granted under this Act to that country's mission or post or to any post connected with it. The Minister's decision in this regard shall be published [?] in the Government Gazette.

Making and enforcing regulations

24. (a) Except for the regulations stated in this Act as required to be made by particular parties, all regulations required to be made under this Act

[stamp] [signature]

shall be made and enforced by the Ministry.

(b) The regulations required to be made under this Act shall be made and published in the Government Gazette within 60 (sixty) days of the commencement of this Act.

Schedules

25. The schedules included in this Act are part of this Act. This Act shall be read together with those schedules.

Commencement of the Act

26. This Act shall commence on the date on which 6 (six) months have elapsed from the date on which this Act is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.

Definitions

27. Unless the manner in which an expression or word is used in this Act specifically conveys another meaning, the following expressions and words shall have the meanings given to them below.

(a) "Privilege" includes the special rights, powers, exemptions, concessions, protection and immunity available to various establishments or posts under this Act.

(b) "Consular post" or "post" means a consulate-general, consulate, vice-consulate or consular agency.

(c) "Diplomatic mission" or "mission" means diplomatic missions established in the Maldives in accordance with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

[stamp] [signature]

(d) "Head of diplomatic mission" means posts appointed and sent by the State to which that mission belongs, with the responsibility of discharging the functions of the head of that mission.

(e) "Maldives Export Import Act" means Law No. 31/79 (Maldives Export Import Act).

(f) "Minister" means the Minister of the government ministry entrusted at the time with the responsibility of implementing the foreign policy of the Maldives.

(g) "Ministry" means the government ministry entrusted at the time with the responsibility of implementing the foreign policy of the Maldives.

(h) "Convention of the Specialised Agencies" means the "Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the Specialized Agencies, 1947".

(i) "Tax Administration Act" means Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act).

(j) "United Nations" means the international organisation established under the Charter of the United Nations.

(k) "Convention on Consular Relations" means the "Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1961".

[stamp] [signature]

(l) "Convention on Diplomatic Relations" means the "Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1963".

(m) "Maldives Customs Service" means the service established under Law No. 8/2011 (Customs Act of the Maldives).

(n) "Maldives Inland Revenue Authority" means the authority established under Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act).
